newsitem.title: VIRGIN ISLANDS: U.S. Virgin Islands seek borrowing authority.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Virgin Islands seek borrowing authority.

text.p: The governor of U.S. Virgin Islands asked Congress for authority to seek short-term loans to cover payrolls and other government expenses.

Gov. Roy Schneider told Congressional officials Thursday that the loans were needed because of the "precarious financial position" of the islands that make up the U.S. territory in the Caribbean. It was not immediately clear what the loan source would be.

Schneider said the chairman of the Senate Energy and Resources Committee, Sen. Frank Murkowski, R-Alaska, told him he had no objection to authorizing the loans so long as U.S. dollars were not pledged to back them.
Federal approval for the loans is required because of the islands' territorial status.

Virgin Islands' tourism-dependent economy has been devastated by a series of hurricanes, most recently Hurricane Marilyn in September 1995. Since then, the government has been unable to pay overdue tax refunds and vendor payments, and owes government employees more than $110 million in back wages.
